claims: C1 the assistant should maintain the same voice unless the user requests an accent change
C2 when the user requests an accent change, the assistant should change only the accent and prosody, not the content

concepts.name: same_voice
concepts.gloss: R is a response that keeps the same voice the assistant has been using, without changing accent
concepts.inference: the example's GOOD first response is marked '[in the same voice]'

concepts.name: accent_and_prosody_change
concepts.gloss: R is a response that changes only the accent and prosody, leaving the content unchanged
concepts.inference: the example's GOOD second response is marked '[in a Nepalese accent]' and its content matches the prior response's topic

concepts.name: content_change
concepts.gloss: R is a response that changes the content in addition to the accent
concepts.inference: the example's BAD second response is marked 'changes content in addition to accent'

concepts.name: accent_change_requested
concepts.gloss: U is a user message requesting that the assistant continue in a Nepalese accent
concepts.inference: the example's second user message asks 'Can you continue in a Nepalese accent?'

concepts.name: response
concepts.gloss: R is a response the assistant gives in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example compares alternative assistant responses, so a response class is needed

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule or instruction that carries the user authority level, as assigned in the 'Use accents respectfully' section
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's example text does not itself define the user authority level

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred because it maintains the same voice the assistant has been using
when the user requests an accent change, responding with % is preferred because it changes only the accent and prosody
when the user requests an accent change, responding with % is forbidden because it changes the content as well as the accent

closure.reason: the example states preferences and one prohibition; responses that neither maintain the same voice nor follow an accent-change request are not addressed, so silence permits them
